question: v09
q: Has eating out got more expensive in Melbourne?

transcript.answer:
Yes. Restaurant meals in Melbourne were **3.3% higher in August 2026 than in August 2025**, according to the ABS Consumer Price Index.

- **Melbourne:** +3.3% year-on-year in August 2026. The rate was 2.5% in April 2025 and peaked at 4.1% in May 2026, so the annual increase has been running between about 2% and 4% over the past year.
- **Australia:** +4.3% year-on-year in August 2026, so Melbourne's restaurant price growth is running slower than the national average.
- **Overall prices:** Melbourne's all-groups CPI was 3.5% in August 2026, so restaurant meals are rising at about the same pace as general inflation in the city.

The series I used is restaurant meals only. I couldn't pull a separate figure for takeaway food, so this doesn't cover all eating out.
